findings.title: Substring matching applies upsampling to mixed or negated Discover queries
findings.body: The eligibility check treats any query containing the text `event.type:error` as error-only. Valid filters such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` and `!event.type:error` therefore enable `upsampled_count()`. Those queries include transaction rows, for which this change explicitly says `sample_weight` is unavailable, so transactions are omitted from the sum (or the query fails depending on the backing schema) and the returned count is incorrect. Determine eligibility from the parsed query and require that all possible branches select sampled error events.

findings.title: Dashboard split queries are checked against the outer dataset instead of the dataset being queried
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` accepts `scoped_dataset`, but the upsampling decision uses the captured outer `dataset` and the original request query. In the metrics-enhanced dashboard split path, the endpoint invokes `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., "(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction", ...)` to retrieve error events while the captured dataset remains a metrics dataset. The helper consequently rejects the query before transformation, and an error-only split widget returns raw sampled counts rather than upsampled counts. Base the decision on `scoped_dataset` and the query argument actually sent to that invocation.

findings.title: Weighted counts are truncated to an integer
findings.body: `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` truncates the aggregate rather than preserving or rounding the sampling estimate. Client sample rates are floats and are not restricted here to rates whose inverse is integral; for example, a 0.3 sample rate produces a non-integral weight. This systematically undercounts such queries, and floating-point accumulation can also turn otherwise integral totals into a value just below the integer boundary. Return the weighted sum as a numeric value or apply the intended explicit rounding rule.

findings.title: The PR adds an unconfigured nested-repository gitlink
findings.body: This adds `sentry-repo` as a gitlink pinned to the base commit, rather than adding source content, and the PR contains no accompanying `.gitmodules` update to define how it can be initialized. Checkouts that initialize submodules can fail or leave this path unpopulated, while the nested repository is unrelated to the feature. Remove this accidental gitlink before merging.
